resources.string: Audio is diverted per app, gain applied, and re-rendered. The faders below are real.
Limited mode — per-app faders are inert
MODIFY_AUDIO_ROUTING is not granted, so nothing can be diverted. Install the Magisk module to move this app into /system/priv-app. System streams below still work.
An app at 100 % is never routed, so it costs nothing. Move a fader and the engine starts.
No apps on the mixer yet
Add the apps you want your own fader for. Anything currently playing shows up here on its own.
Shown while audio is being diverted and re-rendered.
VolumePerApp needs notification-listener access to see which app is playing. It reads no notifications — the permission is the only way to reach getActiveSessions().

Android warns when you raise a headset past its safe level, and lowers the volume on you after a long listen. Both come from one mechanism, so this switch turns off both or neither.

It takes effect when you restart the phone — the platform reads the setting once at boot and never again. The Magisk module applies it.

This removes a hearing protection. Sustained high volume through headphones does cause permanent hearing loss.
Suppressed after you restart the phone
The system warning returns after you restart the phone
Could not record that — the setting is unchanged
None yet. Turning the API on makes one.
New key made. The old one no longer works.
The port must be a number from 1024 to 65535
Lets a script or an agent on this phone do anything the mixer does: move faders, mute, reset, and change settings. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only and needs the key. GET /api/docs describes every route.
PhoneAPI gets its own key, separate from yours, and passes it only to the agents you switch on there. It may do only what you switch on here.
This switches the local API on.
See (every GET): the mixer, your apps\' faders, the streams and the settings
Change (everything else): move faders, mute, reset, set stream volumes and change settings
